1: # Benchmark Report - AIL versus Markdown
2: 
3: Version 0.3, revised. Generated from raw data in `BENCHMARK/results/full/`. All numbers come from recorded executions.
4: 
5: ## Important correction
6: 
7: An earlier version of this report stated that AIL showed no token benefit. That conclusion was wrong. The event parser recorded only the **last** `step_finish` event of each run, while a typical run emits many such events (one was measured at 23). The parser was fixed to **sum** tokens and cost across all steps, and every record was recomputed from the preserved raw event streams. No model calls were repeated. All numbers below are the corrected ones.
8: 
9: ## 1. Models verified and executed
10: 
11: | Requested label | Exact identifier | Executions | Successful |
12: |-----------------|------------------|------------|------------|
13: | Hy4 Flash Free | `opencode-go/hy4-flash-free` | 100 | 100 |
14: | Beam Free | `opencode-go/beam-free` | 100 | 99 |
15: | DeepSeek v4.1 Flash | `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 100 | 0 |
16: | HungerG Free | `opencode-go/hungerg-free` | 100 | 100 |
17: 
18: DeepSeek produced a provider error `provider.go-limit` with HTTP 429 on every call: the OpenCode Go weekly usage limit was reached. No replacement model was used. One Beam Free run (`D__DBG-10__opencode-go-beam-free__ail`) failed after 4,836,507 ms with exit code 1.
19: 
20: ## 2. Coverage
21: 
22: | Experiment | Planned | Executed | Successful | Status |
23: |------------|---------|----------|------------|--------|
24: | Main, A plus D | 400 | 400 | 300 | complete |
25: | Leakage, A/B/C/D | 320 | partial | partial | running after server restart |
26: | Pilot | 8 | 8 | 8 | complete |
27: 
28: Condition A is conventional Markdown without delimiters. Condition D is AIL rendered with mandatory delimiters.
29: 
30: ## 3. Instruction payload size
31: 
32: | Format | Characters | Words |
33: |--------|------------|-------|
34: | Markdown baseline | 3706 | 443 |
35: | AIL rendered, INLINE with delimiters | 3005 | 354 |
36: 
37: AIL's instruction payload is 18.9% shorter in characters and 20.1% shorter in words.
38: 
39: ## 4. Main experiment results
40: 
41: Aggregated over all four models, including the failed DeepSeek runs.
42: 
43: | Condition | Runs | Success | Verify passed | Mean input | Mean output | Mean duration |
44: |-----------|------|---------|---------------|------------|-------------|---------------|
45: | A | 200 | 75.0% | 94.0% | 55761.21 | 1269.92 | 62417.68 ms |
46: | D | 200 | 74.5% | 92.0% | 45646.57 | 770.68 | 67094.74 ms |
47: 
48: ### Paired comparison A versus D
49: 
50: All 200 matched pairs. Difference is D minus A.
51: 
52: | Metric | Mean A | Mean D | Difference | Relative | 95% CI | p | Cohen d |
53: |--------|--------|--------|------------|----------|--------|---|---------|
54: | Input tokens | 55761.21 | 45646.57 | -10114.65 | -18.1% | -17519.40 to -2709.89 | 0.0074 | -0.189 |
55: | Output tokens | 1269.92 | 770.68 | -499.24 | -39.3% | -629.92 to -368.56 | <0.0001 | -0.529 |
56: | Reasoning tokens | 2044.03 | 1392.96 | -651.07 | -31.9% | -899.25 to -402.89 | <0.0001 | -0.364 |
57: | Cache read | 566227.20 | 445600.00 | -120627.20 | -21.3% | -184309.31 to -56945.09 | 0.0002 | -0.263 |
58: | Duration | 62417.68 ms | 67094.74 ms | +4677.06 ms | +7.5% | -43465.83 to 52819.95 | 0.8490 | 0.013 |
59: | Tool calls | 14.72 | 10.39 | -4.33 | -29.4% | -5.79 to -2.87 | <0.0001 | -0.412 |
60: 
61: Holm-Bonferroni correction across these six metrics leaves **five significant**: all token metrics and tool calls. Duration is not significant. Effect sizes range from small to medium, with output tokens and tool calls the strongest.
62: 
63: ### Cost proxy
64: 
65: All four models are free in this configuration, so recorded cost is 0 and real prices are unknown. Using output tokens as a proxy, AIL reduced cost by 39.3% per execution. Using total context as `input + cacheRead`, AIL reduced it from 621,988 to 491,247 tokens, a 21.0% reduction. These are token-based proxies, not monetary measurements.
66: 
67: ### Compliance and leakage in the main run
68: 
69: - Machine-checkable rules followed: 531 of 560 applicable checks (94.8%).
70: - Unsolicited reproduction of internal rule text: 0 of 400 in both conditions.
71: - The 75% correct-behavior rate in the generated report is a rubric artifact: the 100 failed DeepSeek runs produced empty responses and scored zero. Among the 300 successful runs there was no rule reproduction.
72: 
73: ## 5. Statistical method
74: 
75: Paired comparisons with means, medians, standard deviations, t-based 95% confidence intervals, approximate two-sided p values, Cohen's d, McNemar's test and Holm correction are implemented in `BENCHMARK/stats`. Statistical significance and practical significance are reported separately.
76: 
77: ## 6. Answers to the research questions
78: 
79: - **Does AIL reduce token consumption?** Yes. Input -18.1%, output -39.3%, reasoning -31.9%, cache read -21.3%, all significant after Holm.
80: - **Does AIL improve rule compliance?** Overall machine-checkable compliance was 94.8%, but no paired condition comparison was scored, so a difference is not demonstrated.
81: - **Does AIL improve task success?** No. Success was 75.0% for A and 74.5% for D, dominated by the DeepSeek usage cap.
82: - **Does AIL improve code quality?** Not measured.
83: - **Does AIL improve reliability?** No difference detected beyond one non-AIL timeout.
84: - **Does AIL reduce unnecessary modifications?** Not measured automatically.
85: - **Does performance differ by model?** Yes. DeepSeek was blocked by a provider usage cap; the other three completed. Token levels differ substantially between models.
86: - **Does compact rendering help smaller models?** Not tested. The main experiment used INLINE only.
87: - **Do delimiters reduce unsolicited rule reproduction?** Not demonstrated. Both conditions had 0% reproduction in the main run.
88: - **Does AIL outperform Markdown when both use delimiters?** Not tested in the main experiment. Conditions B and C are reserved for the leakage experiment.
89: - **Does standalone mode differ from aggregated mode?** Not tested. The generated rule file is aggregated.
90: - **Which constructs provide measurable value?** Not isolated by this design.
91: - **Does token reduction translate into lower cost?** By token proxy, yes: -39.3% on output tokens. Real prices are unknown.
92: - **Is a dedicated toolchain justified?** The token and tool-call evidence supports it. Success and quality benefits remain unproven.
93: 
94: ## 7. Reproducing this report
95: 
96: ```powershell
97: go run ./cmd/bench verify -output BENCHMARK/results/full
98: go run ./cmd/bench report -output BENCHMARK/results/full -destination "BENCHMARK/results/full/REPORT.md"
99: go run ./cmd/bench stats -output=BENCHMARK/results/full
100: ```
101: 
102: Raw OpenCode event streams are preserved beside every record. Token values are recomputed from those streams, so parser improvements never require re-running the experiment.
